note: 490.3 in E. of the middle of the N. face, §73, the axis of the entrance passage, fixed from a station mark near it. The doorway is lost with the casing and the granite of the passage ends irregularly, so §73 states neither a level nor a distance from the N. base for the beginning of the floor: this east offset is the only coordinate Petrie gives for it. No error stated.

41.29 ± .05 in, §73, the mean of six measures at the mouth, half-way down and near the end (top 41.62, 41.08, 41.34; base 41.21, 41.17, 41.33). §73 remarks that the width is less regular than the height because it depends only on the placing of the side blocks.

47.29 ± .03 in, §73, the mean of six measures on the E. and W. sides (E. 47.33, 47.31, 47.44; W. 47.32, 47.13, 47.23). §73 does not say whether the height is perpendicular or vertical; §38 states the Great Pyramid’s passages as 47 in perpendicularly or 52 in vertically, and 47.29 matches the perpendicular figure.

−5′37″, §73, observed by Prof. Smyth and quoted by Petrie, who did not measure it himself; §93 prints it as −5′37″ ± 10″ with Petrie’s own query mark, and sigma is that 10″. Negative is west of north. §73 notes that it is almost exactly the mean azimuth of the sides, −5′26″.
41.59 ± .04 in, §74, the mean of six measures near the portcullis, beyond the gaps in the floor and near the chamber (top 41.56, 41.65, 41.70; base 41.78, 41.55, 41.30).

71.06 ± .13 in, §74 (E. 70.76, 71.53, 71.27; W. 70.38, 71.36, 71.10); the passage is horizontal, so the perpendicular and the vertical height are the same. The W. reading near the chamber is taken to irregular plastering on the roof. §74 reads the intention as half as high again as the ordinary passage, 71.06 × 2/3 = 47.38 ± .09 against the entrance passage’s 47.29 ± .03.

23.0 in, §74: where the granite walling and roofing ends, the passage roof immediately rises 23.0 in. Added to the entrance passage’s 47.29 that gives 70.3, against the 71.06 ± .13 that §74 measures beyond, so the two statements of the same step differ by about .8 in. No error stated.

11.7 in on the E. and 11.6 on the W., §74, from the end of the sloping roof to the far side of the half-round roll or drum across the roof at the foot of the slope. Stored as the mid of the two readings with sigma covering them.
40.92 in, §74, from the end of the sloping roof to the portcullis groove. No error stated.
41.38 in, §74, the width of the passage at the portcullis. No error stated.

61.11 in, §74, the width across the passage and both portcullis grooves, made up of the 41.38 passage and grooves 9.68 deep on the E. and 10.05 on the W. A single measurement gives 61.14 in front, or N., and 61.35 at back, or S. No error stated.
9.68 in deep on the E., §74, the vertical groove in the granite side of the passage in which the portcullis slab works. No error stated.
10.05 in deep on the W., §74. No error stated.

15.77 in wide on the E., §74; the granite slab of the portcullis is about half an inch thinner than the groove. §74 compares it with the granite leaf of the Great Pyramid, 15.14 to 16.28 thick. No error stated.
15.19 in wide on the W., §74. No error stated.
41.4 to 43.0 in behind the portcullis, §74, where the granite walling and roofing ends and the finely picked limestone begins. Stored as the mid of the range with sigma covering it.
557.9 in, §75, the E. to W. length at the N. wall (Petrie writes 557.9 on N.). The chamber is cut entirely in the rock except for the pointed gable roof of limestone beams. No error stated.
557.4 in at the S. wall, §75. No error stated.
195.8 in, §75, the N. to S. width along the E. wall. No error stated.
195.9 in along the W. wall, §75. No error stated.

206.4 in high at the N.W., with 206.3 and 206.5 (?) at the S.W., §75, the last carrying Petrie’s own query mark. Stored as the mid of 206.3 to 206.5 with sigma covering that range. The floor is partly rock and partly paved, with deep granite blocks around the coffer at the W. end.

244.4 in to the apex of the gable, §75: Vyse gives 38 in for the rise of the gable roof, though measuring the height from the wall base instead of the floor, and Petrie adds that rise to the wall height. No error stated.

About 47 in E. of the Pyramid centre, §73: the entrance passage axis runs 490.3 in E. of the middle of the N. face, and if the horizontal passage keeps the same azimuth as the sloping one, “the chamber lies altogether E. of the Pyramid centre by about 47 inches”. This is the only statement placing the chamber in the Pyramid’s own frame; §75 gives no distance from the centre or from the N. base and no level for the floor. Carrying §75’s doorway, 104.3 to 144.9 from the E. wall, back along the passage axis puts the W. wall nearer 52 in E. of the centre, so the about is doing real work. No error stated.

104.3 in from the E. wall, §75, the E. side of the doorway in the N. wall, which runs 104.3 to 144.9. Stored as a distance from the chamber’s E. wall, which is what Petrie states; he gives no distance from the Pyramid centre. No error stated.
144.9 in from the E. wall, §75, the W. side of the same doorway. No error stated.
103.68 ± .02 in, §77, mean error .04; the readings run 103.62 to 103.73. The coffer is polished inside and out and was let into the floor up to the level of its sliding lid.

41.970 ± .006 in, §77, mean error .015. §77 notes that a coffer 42.0 wide can never have been brought through the passages, which are 41.3 and 41.2 to 41.6 wide, so it was placed before the roof was laid.

38.12 in, §77, marked intended: the height is constant at 38.12 over the whole dressed part of the outside bottom, and lower only where the saw ran too deep and was backed out, one reading giving 37.98. No error stated.
7.645 ± .01 in at the top, §77, mean error .03.

1.70 ± .02 in, §77, mean error .04; the ledge is 1.20 to 2.30 wide on the N. and 1.08 to 1.90 on the S. The lid slid on and was held by undercut grooves along the N., E. and S. sides, and by two pins dropped into resin in the W. side.
103.73 in on the W., §77. The lid lies unbroken on the chamber floor. No error stated.
42.03 in on the S., §77. Its thickness is 9.89 at W.S.W., 8.20 at S.S.W., 8.22 at S. and 8.24 at S.E., so no single thickness is stored. No error stated.
43.1 in at the N. end, §75, from the outside of the coffer to the W. wall of the chamber; §75 adds that the distance was increased by .5 in when the coffer was shifted. No error stated.
42.9 in at the S. end, §75, with the same .5 in of later shifting. No error stated.
42.5 in from the coffer to the N. wall of the chamber, §75. No error stated.
50.0 in from the coffer to the S. wall of the chamber, §75. No error stated.

411.9 in, §78, the E. to W. length at the N. wall (Petrie writes 411.9 on N.) of the lower chamber, cut in the rock below the horizontal passage and plastered. §78 places it by description only, out of the floor of the horizontal passage by a passage descending northwards, so no distance from the Pyramid centre or from the N. base is stated for this chamber anywhere, and no height. No error stated.
411.2 in at the S. wall, §78. No error stated.
123.1 in, §78, the N. to S. width along the E. wall. No error stated.
123.6 in along the W. wall, §78. No error stated.
41.2 in wide, §78, the door in the E. side of the chamber; with 40.9 from the N. and 41.0 from the S. side it divides that side in equal thirds. No error stated.
40.9 in from the N. side, §78, to the door in the E. side. No error stated.
41.0 in from the S. side, §78, to the same door. No error stated.
41.0 in wide at the top, §78, where the short sloping passage into the lower chamber branches from the passage below. No error stated.
41.2 and 41.6 in, §78, the width of the passage from which the sloping passage to the lower chamber branches. Stored as the mid with sigma covering the two readings.
123.8 in long in front, that is on the W., §78, the recess opposite the passage into the lower chamber, cut so that a coffin could be turned into it. No error stated.
122.0 in at back, that is on the E., §78. No error stated.
68.2 in wide on the N., §78, beside the width of the passage, which §78 makes a total of 109.4 on the N. and 109.4 on the S. No error stated.
67.8 in wide on the S., §78. No error stated.

“L’esatto livello della soglia originaria dell’ingresso non è nota, ma se la nostra sezione è accettabile, possiamo fissarla con buona approssimazione a m. 12,90, circa 25 cubiti, sul livello del lastricato del cortile”, p. 53. The doorway went with the casing, so this is a level read off their own reconstructed section and not a measurement of anything still standing, and they say so. Their zero is the pavement of the perimeter courtyard, which p. 105 and p. 108 treat as the base plane of the pyramid, so it is this frame’s zero for G2 as well. No error stated.

“Il corridoio discendente (D) non iniziava nella mezzeria della faccia, ma a m. 12,45 ad est di questa”, p. 53. Petrie’s 490.3 in, 12.45362 m, says the same thing to a centimetre; which of the two a preset uses is the preset’s business. No error stated.

“La lunghezza originale del pavimento del corridoio doveva aggirarsi sui 37 metri”, p. 53, measured along the floor of the descending corridor (D) from the lost doorway in the face down to where the corridor becomes horizontal. The outermost blocks are gone with the casing, so this is the restored length and not the surviving one. No error stated.

The running description gives “La sua inclinazione è di circa 26°46′”, p. 53, and the observation it points at gives “Abbiamo misurato l’inclinazione di (D) in 26°30′ circa”, p. 105, which is their own measurement. The two are stored as their mean, 26°38′, with sigma covering both; the spread is a disagreement inside the volume and not a probable error. p. 105 adds that Hölscher took the intended angle to be 26°35′, a fall of one in two. Negative because the passage descends going away from its beginning at the entrance.

“Abbiamo misurato in m. 11,50 circa l’altezza del limite estremo di questo blocco dal pavimento del cortile”, p. 53: the far, that is the northern, edge of the outermost granite floor block still in place in the descending corridor. It is the highest surviving point of the corridor floor and the only level in it they measured rather than restored, so it is kept as provenance for the 12.90 m threshold above it. No error stated.

“Il piano del pavimento di (L) risulta di circa 3 metri sotto il lastricato del cortile”, p. 55, the short granite-lined horizontal stretch (L) at the foot of the descending corridor, where the portcullis stands. p. 108 states the same the other way round, that the portcullis, (L) and the horizontal corridor (O) are below the base plane of the pyramid. Negative because the frame measures up from that plane. No error stated.

“il corridoio ha ripreso la sua primitiva larghezza di m. 1,05”, p. 55, at the pit (T), past the stretch where the lining stops and the walls are cut rock. Petrie’s 41.59 in, 1.056386 m, is the same width measured in three places. No error stated.

“Non ci risulta che il Petrie abbia corretto la misura di m. 1,17 data dal Perring come distanza della parete sud della cripta dall’asse est-ovest. Accetteremo quindi questo dato con le opportune riserve”, p. 61. Positive, that is north of the east-west axis, because the same page puts the crypt in the north-east quadrant. It is Perring’s figure, not theirs, and they take it with the reservations they state; it is nonetheless the only north-south coordinate any source in the database gives for this chamber. No error stated.

Two sentences together: p. 57 says of the crypt that “il pavimento della parte orientale è costituito da roccia spianata allo stesso livello del corridoio (G)”, and p. 55 puts the floor of the horizontal system about 3 metres below the courtyard pavement, p. 57 adding that (G) comes back at its south end to practically the level of its north end. So the rock floor of the eastern half of the chamber is about 3 m below the base plane. The western half was paved in limestone and granite and was torn up by Perring; p. 109 puts that paving at 35 to 40 cm thick on rock that is 30 to 40 cm lower. Stored as a level rather than left out because it is the only thing that places the chamber vertically, but it is a level read out of two sentences and not a figure either author printed, which is why it is the one record here left unverified. No error stated.

“come altezza delle pareti m. 5,24 (10 cubiti)”, p. 59, Vandier’s figure, which Maragioglio and Rinaldi adopt for their own drawings. It is Petrie’s 206.4 in rounded to the centimetre and converted, so it is not independent of him. No error stated.

“come altezza massima all’apice m. 6,84 (circa 13 cubiti)”, p. 59, again Vandier’s, and “Sono queste le misure da noi adottate nei disegni”. p. 59 spends a paragraph rejecting the two figures the database already carries: Perring’s 6.83 m apex over 5.87 m walls, which leaves a gable of 0.96 m that his own section contradicts by drawing at least 1.57 m, and Petrie’s 244.4 in, which is his measured wall height plus Perring’s bad 38 in difference. Height above the chamber floor, like every gable height here. No error stated.

“pendenza dei travi 34°10′”, p. 59, Vandier’s pitch for the butting limestone beams of the roof, adopted with the two heights beside it. Nothing builds from it: the chamber is drawn from its floor, its wall height and the ridge above them, so the pitch is provenance and a check on the other two. No error stated.

“questo secondo ingresso è posto esattamente in corrispondenza dell’ingresso superiore, così che tutto il sistema di passaggi interni è sul medesimo piano verticale”, p. 61, of the second entrance at the foot of the north face, whose mouth was covered by the paving of the perimeter courtyard. Being in the same vertical plane as the upper entrance gives it the same 12.45 m that p. 53 puts east of the middle of the face, and nothing else: p. 61 states no distance out from the pyramid and no level for it, only that its mouth lay under the paving. Check it against p. 61 and p. 53 together. No error stated.

“si entra nel corridoio (I), di sezione praticamente uguale a quella di (A), che porta nel cortile perimetrale con una inclinazione di circa 22°40′”, p. 63. Negative because the corridor begins at the lower entrance in the courtyard and descends southwards into the rock; p. 63 describes it in the other direction, coming out into the courtyard. No error stated.

Of the horizontal corridor (P), “Esso è più alto di (A) raggiungendo i m. 1,83, ma ne conserva la stessa larghezza di 2 cubiti”, p. 61. The width is given in cubits and not in metres, so it is not entered: a cubit is itself a quantity this database argues about. The same page gives 1.64 m for the rough recess opposite the branch to the lower chamber. No error stated.

“Il passaggio (A) scende verso nord con una inclinazione non perfettamente costante che risulta essere, in media, 21°40′”, p. 61. Positive because the corridor is taken from its northern end, where it leaves the horizontal corridor (P), and rises southwards to the pit (T) in the floor of the upper horizontal corridor; that is the way it is walked from the lower entrance and the way p. 61 names it, the lower ascending corridor. The mean of an inclination that p. 61 says is not constant. No error stated.

“Abbiamo misurato come altezza verticale m. 1,30 − 1,34 e come altezza perpendicolare alla pendenza m. 1,21 − 1,235”, p. 61. The perpendicular pair is the one stored, because a passage here is extruded square to its floor, and it is stored as the mid of 1.21 to 1.235 with sigma covering the pair. p. 61 puts the varying height down to the varying slope of the floor. No probable error stated.
